Repo: https://github.com/clawdbot/clawdbot. Source: `src/` (`src/cli`, `src/commands`, `src/provider-web.ts`, `src/infra`, `src/media`); colocated `*.test.ts`; docs `docs/`; built output `dist/`; plugins `extensions/*`. Keep plugin-only deps in the extension `package.json`; do not add them to the root `package.json` unless core uses them. Installers served from `https://clawd.bot/*` live in `../clawd.bot` (`public/install.sh`, `public/install-cli.sh`, `public/install.ps1`).

Always consider **all** built-in + extension channels when refactoring shared logic (routing, allowlists, pairing, command gating, onboarding, docs). Core docs: `docs/channels/`; core code: `src/telegram`, `src/discord`, `src/slack`, `src/signal`, `src/imessage`, `src/web`, `src/channels`, `src/routing`; extensions include `extensions/msteams`, `extensions/matrix`, `extensions/zalo`, `extensions/zalouser`, `extensions/voice-call`.

Mintlify docs (`docs.clawd.bot`): internal `docs/**/*.md` links are root-relative, without `.md`/`.mdx` (e.g. `[Config](/configuration)`); cross-references use anchors (e.g. `[Hooks](/configuration#hooks)`). When Peter asks for links, reply with full `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs (not root-relative). When you touch docs, end the reply with the `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs you referenced. README links must be absolute docs URLs. Docs content must be generic: no personal device names/hostnames/paths; use placeholders like `user@gateway-host` and “gateway host”.

Node **22+**; keep Node + Bun paths working. Install: `pnpm install`; also `bun install` (keep `pnpm-lock.yaml` + Bun patching in sync when touching deps/patches). Prefer Bun for TypeScript execution: `bun <file.ts>` / `bunx <tool>`. CLI dev: `pnpm clawdbot ...` or `pnpm dev`. Node supports built output (`dist/*`) and production installs. Build/type-check: `pnpm build`; lint: `pnpm lint`; format: `pnpm format`; tests: `pnpm test`; coverage: `pnpm test:coverage`. TypeScript ESM; prefer strict typing, avoid `any`. Run `pnpm lint` before commits. Run `pnpm test` (or `pnpm test:coverage`) before pushing when you touch logic. Framework: Vitest, V8 coverage thresholds (70% lines/branches/functions/statements); tests `*.test.ts`, e2e `*.e2e.test.ts`. Live: `CLAWDBOT_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live` or `LIVE=1 pnpm test:live`; Docker: `pnpm test:docker:live-models`, `pnpm test:docker:live-gateway`; onboarding: `pnpm test:docker:onboard`. Full kit: `docs/testing.md`. Pure test additions/fixes generally do **not** need a changelog entry unless they alter user-facing behavior or the user asks for one.

Use Clawdbot for product/app/docs headings; `clawdbot` for CLI, package/binary, paths, config keys. Keep files concise; extract helpers instead of “V2” copies. Use existing CLI option patterns and dependency injection via `createDefaultDeps`. Add brief comments for tricky logic. Aim under ~700 LOC; keep files under ~500 LOC when feasible. Oxlint/Oxfmt. Releases: stable tagged `vYYYY.M.D`, npm `latest`; beta `vYYYY.M.D-beta.N`, npm `beta`; dev is moving `main`, no tag. Changelog: latest released version at top, no `Unreleased`; after publishing, bump version and start a new top section.

Mobile: before using a simulator, check for connected real devices (iOS + Android) and prefer them when available. Before testing, verify connected real devices (iOS/Android) before reaching for simulators/emulators. Commits: `scripts/committer "<msg>" <file...>`; avoid manual `git add`/`git commit` so staging stays scoped. Use concise action-oriented messages; group related changes and avoid unrelated refactors. PRs summarize scope, testing, user-facing changes/new flags.

PR review: given a PR link, use `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`; do **not** change branches. Prefer one `gh pr view --json ...` for metadata/comments; run `gh pr diff` only when needed. Before starting a review when a GH Issue/PR is pasted: run `git pull`; if there are local changes or unpushed commits, stop and alert the user before reviewing. **Review mode (PR link only):** read `gh pr view/diff`; **do not** switch branches; **do not** change code.
PR merge: create a temp/integration branch from `main`; bring in PR commits (prefer squash unless history matters; landing mode prefers rebase for linear history, merge allowed when safer). Always try to merge unless truly difficult. Apply fixes, add changelog entry (+ thanks + PR #), run full gate locally before committing: `pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm test`; commit, merge back to `main`, delete temp branch, then `git switch main` (never stay on a topic branch after landing). Contributor needs to be in git graph. If squash, add PR author as co-contributor. If you review a PR and later do work on it, land via merge/squash (no direct-main commits) and always add the PR author as a co-contributor. When working on a PR: add a changelog entry with the PR number and thank the contributor. When working on an issue: reference the issue in the changelog entry. When merging a PR: leave a PR comment explaining exactly what we did and include SHA hashes. For a new contributor, add their avatar to README “Thanks to all clawtributors”; after merging, run `bun scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` if missing, then commit regenerated README. When working on a GitHub Issue or PR, print the full URL at the end of the task.
`sync`: if working tree is dirty, commit all changes (pick a sensible Conventional Commit message), then `git pull --rebase`; if rebase conflicts and cannot resolve, stop; otherwise `git push`.

Never commit or publish real phone numbers, videos, or live configuration values. Use obviously fake placeholders in docs, tests, and examples. Never edit `node_modules` (global/Homebrew/npm/git installs too). Skill notes go in `tools.md` or `AGENTS.md`. Never update the Carbon dependency. Any dependency with `pnpm.patchedDependencies` must use an exact version (no `^`/`~`). Patching dependencies (pnpm patches, overrides, or vendored changes) requires explicit approval; do not do this by default.

Web creds: `~/.clawdbot/credentials/`; rerun `clawdbot login` if logged out. Pi sessions default `~/.clawdbot/sessions/`; base directory is not configurable. Environment variables: `~/.profile`. Rebrand/migration or legacy config/service warnings: run `clawdbot doctor` (see `docs/gateway/doctor.md`). “makeup” = “mac app”.

Gateway runs only as menubar app; no separate LaunchAgent/helper label. Restart via Clawdbot Mac app or `scripts/restart-mac.sh`; verify/kill with `launchctl print gui/$UID | grep clawdbot`, not a fixed label. **When debugging on macOS, start/stop the gateway via the app, not ad-hoc tmux sessions; kill any temporary tunnels before handoff.** Logs: `./scripts/clawlog.sh`; supports follow/tail/category filters and expects passwordless sudo for `/usr/bin/log`. If shared guardrails are available locally, review them; otherwise follow this repo's guidance.

SwiftUI iOS/macOS: prefer `Observation` framework (`<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`) over `ObservableObject`/`<REDACTED_USER>`; don’t introduce new `ObservableObject` unless required for compatibility, and migrate existing usages when touching related code. New connection: update every UI surface and docs (macOS app, web UI, mobile if applicable, onboarding/overview docs) and add matching status + configuration form
